# what: a measurement of triage.py's own invalid-probe classifier, not of dxc
# how:  cd .github/skills/dxc-issue-triage && python data/issues/2792/classifier-probe.py
# ran:  2026-08-07T05:02:00+00:00
# why:  #2792's symptom is a MISSING diagnostic, so its predicate must express
#       an absence. Sections A/B exercise the shipped predicate, C the naive
#       absence-only predicate, D the _predicate_quotes suppression, E the
#       positive anchor that match.json actually uses. See method-notes.md.
# note: sections B, C and E feed synthetic or borrowed text to classify() on
#       purpose -- they measure the classifier, and only section A's inputs are
#       real captures of repro.hlsl/controls.
==============================================================================

==============================================================================

    -> verdict     : repro

    -> verdict     : repro

==============================================================================
B. Hypothetical future DXC that FIXES #2792 by emitting the diagnostic.
   Scores no-repro (correct). Is it then demoted by the marker rule?
==============================================================================

  plain wording
    predicate      : match.json (absence-shaped: True)
    exit           : 0x80004005   internal_failure: False
    -> verdict     : no-repro

  validator wording, mirroring the existing RS check
    predicate      : match.json (absence-shaped: True)
    exit           : 0x80004005   internal_failure: False
    -> verdict     : no-repro

  wording that merely mentions the target -- does NOT trip a marker
    predicate      : match.json (absence-shaped: True)
    exit           : 0x80004005   internal_failure: False
    -> verdict     : no-repro

  gated wording -- DOES trip the 'requires shader model' marker
    predicate      : match.json (absence-shaped: True)
    exit           : 0x80004005   internal_failure: False
    -> verdict     : invalid-probe
    -> reason      : output matched the feature-absence marker "requires shader model", so this build did not reach the code under test

==============================================================================
C. The trap this issue is exposed to: a NAIVE absence-only predicate
   ('no error mentions the root constant size'), which is what an
   absence predicate for this issue looks like without a positive
   anchor. Fed REAL output from an input dxc genuinely rejected.
==============================================================================

  control-rs-register-mismatch under the naive predicate
    predicate      : classifier-probe-naive-predicate.json (absence-shaped: True)
    exit           : 0x80004005   internal_failure: False
    -> verdict     : repro

  a bare syntax error under the naive predicate
    predicate      : classifier-probe-naive-predicate.json (absence-shaped: True)
    exit           : 0x80004005   internal_failure: False
    -> verdict     : repro

  a release that cannot express the input (marker present)
    predicate      : classifier-probe-naive-predicate.json (absence-shaped: True)
    exit           : 0x80004005   internal_failure: False
    -> verdict     : invalid-probe
    -> reason      : an absence clause of this predicate can be satisfied for free by a run that failed early (matched "invalid profile")

  a release that crashed
    predicate      : classifier-probe-naive-predicate.json (absence-shaped: True)
    exit           : 0xC0000005   internal_failure: True
    -> verdict     : invalid-probe
    -> reason      : an absence clause of this predicate can be satisfied for free by a run that failed early (the probe failed internally)

==============================================================================
D. _predicate_quotes suppression -- the #3055 fix -- on this issue
==============================================================================

  positive clauses of match.json: ['extractvalue %dx\\.types\\.CBufRet\\.f32 [^,\\n]+, 1\\b']
  _predicate_quotes('is not supported for the target') = False
  _predicate_quotes('use of undeclared identifier') = False
  _predicate_quotes('invalid profile') = False

  The suppression requires a positive clause of the issue's own
  predicate to quote the marker verbatim. #2792 asks for a diagnostic
  that does not exist in any DXC, so there is no text to quote and the
  suppression is structurally unavailable here.

==============================================================================
E. The mitigation actually used by match.json: anchor the absence with
   a positive clause. Same four inputs as section C.
==============================================================================

  control-rs-register-mismatch under the anchored predicate
    predicate      : classifier-probe-anchored-predicate.json (absence-shaped: True)
    exit           : 0x80004005   internal_failure: False
    -> verdict     : no-repro

  a bare syntax error under the anchored predicate
    predicate      : classifier-probe-anchored-predicate.json (absence-shaped: True)
    exit           : 0x80004005   internal_failure: False
    -> verdict     : no-repro

  a release that cannot express the input
    predicate      : classifier-probe-anchored-predicate.json (absence-shaped: True)
    exit           : 0x80004005   internal_failure: False
    -> verdict     : invalid-probe
    -> reason      : output matched the feature-absence marker "invalid profile", so this build did not reach the code under test

  a release that crashed
    predicate      : classifier-probe-anchored-predicate.json (absence-shaped: True)
    exit           : 0xC0000005   internal_failure: True
    -> verdict     : invalid-probe
    -> reason      : the probe failed internally, so it measured nothing about the reported symptom

  All four score no-repro or invalid-probe -- never a false `repro`.
  The anchor, not the classifier, is what makes this issue safe.
